extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in analytic number theory or complex analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, estimates and proofs concerning analytic properties of the Gamma function, its reciprocal, the Riemann zeta function, their functional equations, product factorizations, growth estimates, zeros, and reductions used in the prime number theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal Gamma is entire with simple zeros at nonpositive integers
rubrics_metrics.description: 1/Γ(s) is entire; the simple poles of Γ(1 − s) at s = 1,2,3,... are cancelled by zeros of sin πs so 1/Γ has simple zeros at s = 0, −1, −2, −3, ... and vanishes nowhere else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the identity 1/Γ(s) = Γ(1 − s) sin πs / π to see pole-zero cancellation. This characterization (entire, simple zeros at nonpositive integers, no other zeros) plus growth order ≤ 1 essentially determines 1/Γ up to normalizing factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth bound for 1/Γ(s) (order 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist constants c1, c2 so that |1/Γ(s)| ≤ c1 e^{c2 |s| log |s|}. Consequently 1/Γ is of order 1: for every ε > 0 there is a bound c(ε) with |1/Γ(s)| ≤ c(ε) e^{c2 |s|^{1+ε}}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive from representation (5) and estimates on Γ(1−s), sin πs, and integrals like ∫_0^∞ e^{-t} t^{-s} dt. The argument splits cases depending on Im(s) large or small and uses bounds |sin πs| ≤ e^{π|s|} and integral estimates e^{(|σ|+1) log(|σ|+1)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weierstrass product for 1/Γ(s) (product formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all s ∈ C, 1/Γ(s) = e^{γ s} s ∏_{n=1}^∞ (1 + s/n) e^{-s/n}, where γ is Euler's constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Hadamard factorization to the entire function 1/Γ of order 1 with simple zeros at 0, −1, −2, ...; determine multiplicative constants by evaluating limits like sΓ(s) → 1 as s → 0 and Γ(1)=1. The proof shows uniqueness up to factors e^{As+B} and fixes A=γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and existence of Euler's constant γ
rubrics_metrics.description: γ = lim_{N→∞} (Σ_{n=1}^N 1/n − log N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence shown by comparing harmonic sums with integrals and using the mean value theorem to bound differences by 1/n^2; used to fix constant in the 1/Γ product formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: ζ(s) series definition and region of convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: ζ(s) = Σ_{n=1}^∞ n^{−s} converges for Re(s) > 1 and defines a holomorphic function there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate |n^{−s}| = n^{−σ} and use comparison with Σ 1/n^{1+δ} for σ > 1 + δ to conclude uniform convergence on half-planes Re(s) > 1 + δ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral relation linking ζ, Γ and theta function (Theorem 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by termwise integrating ∫_0^∞ e^{-π n^2 u} u^{s/2−1} du = π^{-s/2} Γ(s/2) n^{-s} and interchanging sum and integral justified by growth/decay estimates of ϑ(u).

rubrics_metrics.name: Xi-function and functional equation (analytic continuation of ζ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ξ(s)=π^{-s/2} Γ(s/2) ζ(s). Then ξ is holomorphic for Re(s)>1 and continues meromorphically to C with simple poles at s=0 and s=1; moreover ξ(s)=ξ(1−s), giving the functional equation for ζ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theta functional equation ϑ(u)=u^{-1/2}ϑ(1/u), split integrals, handle n=0 separately, and show the resulting integral defines an entire function; symmetry under s→1−s produces functional equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meromorphic continuation of ζ(s) with only pole at s=1
rubrics_metrics.description: ζ(s) extends meromorphically to all of C and its only singularity is a simple pole at s=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From ξ(s) analytic continuation and ξ(s)=π^{-s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s) use that 1/Γ(s/2) is entire with zeros at 0,−2,−4,... to cancel the pole of ξ at s=0; conclude ζ has sole pole at s=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation of partial sums by integrals and δ_n(s) (Proposition 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist entire functions δ_n(s) with |δ_n(s)| ≤ |s|/n^{σ+1} (σ=Re(s)) such that Σ_{1≤n<N} n^{−s} − ∫_1^N x^{−s} dx = Σ_{1≤n<N} δ_n(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define δ_n(s) = ∫_n^{n+1} (n^{−s} − x^{−s}) dx and use mean value theorem to bound integrand by |s|/n^{σ+1}. Summing yields analytic continuation into Re(s)>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition ζ(s) − 1/(s−1) is holomorphic for Re(s)>0 (Corollary 2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Re(s)>0 one has ζ(s) − 1/(s − 1) = H(s) where H(s)=Σ_{n=1}^∞ δ_n(s) is holomorphic in Re(s)>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let N→∞ in the identity of Proposition 2.5 and use the δ_n(s) bounds to conclude uniform convergence and holomorphy for Re(s)>0; this isolates the simple pole at s=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth estimates for ζ(s) near Re(s)=1 (Proposition 2.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If s=σ+it and 0 ≤ σ0 ≤ 1, then for every ε>0 there exists c(ε) such that (i) |ζ(s)| ≤ c(ε) |t|^{1−σ0+ε} for σ0 ≤ σ and |t| ≥ 1, and (ii) |ζ^{(k)}(s)| ≤ c(ε) |t|^{ε} for σ ≥ 1 and |t| ≥ 1 (suitable k; text gives a consequence for ζ and its derivatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Corollary 2.6 with δ_n estimates, combine two bounds |δ_n(s)| ≤ |s|/n^{σ+1} and |δ_n(s)| ≤ 2/n^σ via Hölder-type interpolation to get decay in n; choose parameters δ and combine with Cauchy integral formula to bound derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler product for ζ and nonvanishing for Re(s)>1
rubrics_metrics.description: For Re(s)>1, ζ(s)=∏_p (1 − p^{−s})^{−1}. From this product ζ(s) ≠ 0 when Re(s)>1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify by expanding geometric series for each prime and using unique factorization to relate product of prime-power series to Σ n^{−s}. Absolute convergence in Re(s)>1 allows rearrangement and taking logs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of 'trivial' zeros: negative even integers (Theorem 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: All zeros of ζ(s) outside the critical strip 0 ≤ Re(s) ≤ 1 are the negative even integers −2, −4, −6, ... (the trivial zeros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From functional equation ζ(s)=π^{s−1/2} Γ((1−s)/2)/Γ(s/2) ζ(1−s). For Re(s)<0, ζ(1−s) nonzero, Γ((1−s)/2) zero-free, and 1/Γ(s/2) has zeros at s=−2,−4,... so these are the only zeros in Re(s)<0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonvanishing of ζ on the line Re(s)=1 (Theorem 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: ζ(1 + it) ≠ 0 for all real t (i.e., ζ has no zeros on the line Re(s)=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key ingredients: expansion log ζ(s)=Σ_{p,m} p^{−m s}/m with nonnegative coefficients; inequality 3 + 4 cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 gives positivity of log |ζ^3(σ) ζ^4(σ+it) ζ(σ+2it)|; contradiction argument if a zero existed at 1+it0 using known pole at s=1 and behavior of ζ near 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logarithmic expansion of ζ (Lemma 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Re(s)>1, log ζ(s) = Σ_{p,m} p^{−m s}/m = Σ_{n=1}^∞ c_n n^{−s} for some c_n ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take logarithm of Euler product and use log(1/(1−x))=Σ_{m≥1} x^m/m (valid for |x|<1) to get double sum; absolute convergence permits rearrangement and definition of c_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positivity trick via trigonometric inequality (Lemma 1.4 and Corollary 1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For real θ, 3 + 4 cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0; hence for σ>1 and real t, log |ζ^3(σ) ζ^4(σ+it) ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain lower bounds that force contradictions if ζ had zeros on Re(s)=1. Translate cos(t log n) appearances in Re(log ζ(s)) into the inequality and sum with nonnegative weights c_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative lower bound for |ζ(σ+it)| when σ≥1 (Proposition 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every ε>0 there is c(ε) so that 1/|ζ(s)| ≤ c(ε) |t|^{ε} when s=σ+it with σ ≥ 1 and |t| ≥ 1 (equivalently |ζ(σ+it)| ≥ c'(σ−1)^{3/4} |t|^{-C} etc.; text gives an explicit derivation yielding a power of |t|).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine positivity bound |ζ^3(σ) ζ^4(σ+it) ζ(σ+2it)| ≥ 1 with growth estimates for ζ from Proposition 2.7 to infer a lower bound for |ζ(σ+it)|. Handle two cases depending on whether σ−1 is larger or smaller than a chosen A|t|^{-5ε}, and use mean value theorem to control differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of Chebyshev's ψ and Λ
rubrics_metrics.description: ψ(x) = Σ_{p^m ≤ x} log p = Σ_{n≤x} Λ(n), where Λ(n)=log p if n=p^m and 0 otherwise; ψ(x)=Σ_{p≤x} [log x / log p] log p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ψ carries weighted prime-power information and is monotone increasing; alternate forms (sum over prime powers and over primes with integer part) are useful for linking ζ to prime counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of ψ(x)∼x and π(x)∼x/log x (Proposition 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ψ(x) ∼ x as x→∞, then π(x) ∼ x / log x as x→∞ (converse true but omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elementary inequalities: relate ψ(x) to π(x) via ψ(x) ≤ π(x) log x and ψ(x) ≥ (π(x)−π(x^α)) log x^α to squeeze π(x) and obtain limsup/liminf bounds; choose α→1 to conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to integrated ψ (ψ1) (Proposition 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ψ1(x)=∫_1^x ψ(u) du ∼ x^2/2 as x→∞, then ψ(x) ∼ x and hence π(x) ∼ x/log x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monotonicity of ψ and averaging: for α<1<β, bound ψ(x) between scaled differences of ψ1 on [αx,x] and [x,βx]; apply asymptotics on ψ1 to derive bounds for ψ(x)/x and let β→1.
